chapter_theme: Two songs at Thirukkudavayil (திருக்குடவாயில்): a plea to be freed from the price-women and from mala, maya and the gunas, and a song of wonder at Murugan as everything, the guru who made the poet speak of him, praised as the child of Uma who came as the Kauniya brahmin and sent the disputants to the stake.
structure_note: 836 is the usual plea and praise; 837 has no confession at all: its first half lists what Murugan is, and its second tells the Sambandar story.

836.reading: The poet speaks of the price-women with spear-like kohl eyes whom strangers court, deceivers even as they lie on the bed, and asks that his wandering infatuation end, that mala, maya and the gunas change, and that by the Veda he gain grace and the wondrous feet sweet as a honey garland. The praise names Murugan who gave the meaning as a command to the lord of Kailasa, who threw the bright vel at old Sura hiding in the sea, the clever lover of the Kurava girl, at Kudavayil among groves where cuckoos sing.
836.nuance: கயிலாயப்பதி உடையாருக்கு ஒரு பொருளே கட்டளை இடுவோனே: Murugan does not merely explain the meaning to Siva but lays it down as a command, the guru over the father. மறையால் மிக்கருள் பெறவே, grace through the Veda, is an unusual route for this poet, who more often asks grace through song or devotees; the phrase may also be read otherwise.

837.reading: The poet marvels that Murugan, who is the Veda, grammar and the many languages, beginning and middle, renunciation, dharma and the path, the joy of the wise, cloud and rain, sun, moon and stars, space and light, beyond day and night, the supreme maya none can know, became his guru and made him speak of it, and wonders whether this is the fruit of some first day. The praise tells how Murugan came as the Kauniya brahmin child who drank Uma's milk, a poet beyond all singers, sent the disputants to the stake, spread holy ash, straightened the cruel Maran's hunch and made Madurai flourish, and dwells at Kudasai.
837.nuance: The second half is the story of Sambandar told as Murugan's own: கவுணியர் குல வேதியன், the child who drank உமை's milk, the வாதிகள் impaled, the Pandya கூன் straightened, ash applied (நீறிட), all unmistakable details. நீ குருவாய் இது பகருமாறு செய்தாய் suggests the poet's own song is the guru's gift, a thanksgiving rather than a plea. The long list of what Murugan becomes is the pervasion the Tirumanthiram calls வியாபகம்.

links.note: Both credit the poet's singing to Murugan's own teaching: in 2 Murugan told him to sing the Thiruppugazh; in 837 he 'became guru and made me speak this', which the poet wonders at as the fruit of some former day.

836 calls the price-women deceivers even while they lie on the bed (அணைமீதில் துயில் பொழுதே தெட்டிகள்). Kural 913 says the false embrace of women of wealth (பொருட்பெண்டிர் பொய்ம்மை முயக்கம்) is like embracing a stranger's corpse in a dark room. Both locate the deceit in the embrace itself, the place where trust would be greatest; the Kural gives it its grim image.

837 marvels that Murugan is the Veda, cloud and rain, sun and moon and stars, space and light (முகிலாய் மழையாய் ... பருதியாய் மதியாய் ... வெளியாய் ஒளியாய்) and became the poet's guru. Tirumanthiram 10 says he himself bears the earth and is the sky, fire, sun and moon, the rain-pouring lady, mountain and sea (தானே ... ஞாயிறும் திங்களும் தானே மழைபொழி தையலுமாய்). The song applies to Murugan the litany of pervasion the Tirumanthiram opens with, adding scripture and dharma to the elements.
